title: dxi-mcp-server: Detect AppData connector credential fields from toolkit schema.json for out-of-band secure capture

acceptance_criteria.text: For an AppData operation (e.g. DB2 or MySQL dSource link / VDB provision) on a capture-capable host, every connector parameter declared "format": "password" in the toolkit schema.json triggers sensitive_input_required when missing or supplied inline. This includes nested properties.
The DCT AI Assistant shows the secure credential UI for those fields, and the value reaches DCT without entering the LLM context.
Re-calls with the field supplied via sensitive_applied (valid nonce) succeed and do not re-prompt (no regression of DLPXECO-14603).
Non-password connector fields (usernames, ports, paths, ids) are never flagged.
Native (non-AppData) operations behave exactly as today, still driven by x-dct-toolkit-credential-field.
Non-capture-capable clients (Claude Desktop/Code, VS Code Copilot) behave as today. The gate stays host-scoped (DLPXECO-14642).
If the toolkit schema can't be fetched or parsed, the server logs a warning and falls back to spec-annotation-only behaviour. The operation is not blocked.
Unit tests cover the schema walker (nested, arrays, combinators, $ref), path-scoped matching, caching and fallback. Integration tests cover at least DB2 and MySQL toolkits.

sensitive_input_required returns each flagged field's location in the request (e.g. appdata_source_params.dbPassword), alongside today's required_sensitive_fields names, which stay for backward compatibility. Exact shape to be agreed with DLPXECO-14782.
sensitive_applied.fields (from the host) is matched by location as well as by name, so injected connector fields are not flagged again.

constraints.text: required_sensitive_fields names must remain in sensitive_input_required response for backward compatibility — new location-keyed fields are additions, not replacements.
Must not regress DLPXECO-14603: re-calls with sensitive_applied (valid nonce) must not re-prompt.
Native (non-AppData) credential detection via x-dct-toolkit-credential-field must remain unchanged.
Host scoping from DLPXECO-14642 must remain: gate only fires for capture-capable hosts.
If the toolkit schema can't be fetched or parsed, fall back gracefully to spec-annotation-only — do not block the operation.
Cache derived credential set per toolkit (id + version) to avoid re-fetching schema on every call.
Path-scoped matching: connector password fields must be matched relative to the AppData parameters sub-object, not globally by name.

decisions.text:
- Absent connector password fields are flagged only when schema-required, outside oneOf/anyOf-only branches, with parent object present; present ones are always flagged.
- Connector secret detection relies solely on exact "format": "password"; no name heuristics and no identity-pairing for connector fields.
- New sensitive_input_required location data is additive (proposed key sensitive_field_locations: [{name, location}]), pending agreement with DLPXECO-14782.
- Toolkit resolution unions body toolkit_id and referenced-object toolkit so a caller-supplied id can never narrow detection.
- Discovery secret marking and all toolkit lookups only occur on capture-capable hosts.
